subject: population-health-and-ethics
title: Australian health system: Medicare and PBS

steps.tx: Australia funds most health care through **Medicare**, a universal public scheme. Medicare Benefits Schedule items pay rebates for doctor and some allied services. The **Pharmaceutical Benefits Scheme** (PBS) subsidises listed medicines, so patients pay a capped co-payment rather than the full price. Both are federal programmes, and the exam tests which pathway funds which service.

steps.tx: Medicare rebates for allied health need a **GP management plan** or **team care arrangement** for patients with chronic or complex conditions. The GP assesses, sets goals and documents the team. Without this written plan, sessions with a dietitian, podiatrist or diabetes educator are not rebated. Plans are time limited and reviewed regularly.

steps.tx: The **Safety Net** protects families from high cumulative costs. Co-payments for all PBS scripts for a family count towards a threshold, and must be recorded through the pharmacy. Once the threshold is reached, the rest of the year's PBS scripts cost less. Concession card holders have a lower threshold than general patients.

steps.tx: For long-term users, cumulative co-payments build up across the year, so recording every script matters. A **mental health treatment plan** is the separate GP pathway for rebated psychology sessions. Private health insurance does not replace PBS subsidies or Medicare rebates. Medicare rebates are paid per service, not per year.
